newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips gain in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips gain in active trade.

text.p: Blue chip stocks made strong gains in brisk Thursday trading on the Nigerian stock exchange, dealers said.
The all-share index had not been updated by 1900 (1800 GMT).
Traders said growing confidence in the economy had pushed banks, food, oil and textile shares.
The half-yearly budget review from finance minister Anthony Ani came too late to affect trade. Ani forecast the economy would grow at least 4.94 percent through 1996.
He also said the government would pay off 5.0 billion naira owed to local companies by the third quarter of 1996.
Union Bank's good run continued as shares rose 10 kobo to 6.90 naira. UBA and Trade Bank each gained two kobo to close at 5.44 naira and 1.45 naira, respectively.
National Oil gained 18 kobo to 27.20 naira. Both Texaco and Unipetrol gained 15 kobo, closing at 23.58 naira and 34.15 naira, respectively.

Flour Mills Nigeria added 15 kobo to 8.70 naira. Cadbury closed 10 kobo up at 23.38 naira, the same margin as Lever Brothers, which finished at 24.20 naira and West African Portland Cement at 27.95 naira. John Holt was the conglomerate sector's sole faller, dropping five kobo to 11.35 naira.
Private airline ADC fell eight kobo to 5.30 naira. Chemical firm CAP also fell eight kobo to close at 5.80 naira.
First Aluminium fell four kobo to 5.35 naira, while Vitafoam closed two kobo lower at 5.36 naira as investors dumped them following their recent weak-looking performances.
Cement Company of Northern Nigerian adjusted for dividend, closing 65 kobo down at 2.30 naira. ($1=80 naira)
